newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: U.S. promises Guatemala $50 million in peace aid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. promises Guatemala $50 million in peace aid.

text.p: The United States announced on Monday an immediate $15.5 million cash gift as part of a long-term $50 million aid package for Guatemala to support the implementation of recently signed peace accords.

"This is an initial promise from the United States to give an amount no less than $50 million in special financing to carry out peace accords, above and beyond our normal assistance programmes for Guatemala," U.S. Ambassador Donald Planty told a news conference.
The Guatemalan government and the leftist rebels of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit signed a historic peace treaty on Dec. 29, ending 36 years of civil war.
The peace accords contain ambitious social and economic programmes designed to correct the poverty and injustice at the roots of the war, which left an estimated 140,000 dead or missing.
The money from the United States will go toward health, education and rural infrastructure projects in parts of Guatemala affected by years of violent conflict.

Mark Schneider, assistant administrator of the U.S. Agency for International Development, said the new money is in addition to regular economic aid programmes for Guatemala, bringing Guatemala's annual U.S. aid level to $40 million, where it will remain for the next few years.
In Washington, the United States said on Monday it was "very disappointed" that China vetoed a U.N. plan to monitor disarmament and a ceasefire in Guatemala as it ended its civil war.

All Security Council members except China voted on Friday for a resolution that would have dispatched 155 peacekeepers to Guatemala for three months under a U.N.-brokered peace accord signed on Dec. 29 between the government and leftist rebels.
But China vetoed the move because of Guatemala's diplomatic ties with Taiwan, which Beijing considers a renegade province.
